This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The reported issue is an OutOfMemoryError when using ExtendedMessageFormat with a custom format registry and a pattern containing single quotes.

The test under failure creates an ExtendedMessageFormat instance with a pattern that contains escaped single quotes: "it''s a {0,lower} 'test'!" and passes a custom format registry.

Looking at the ExtendedMessageFormat constructor, the pattern is passed to applyPattern. The applyPattern method is responsible for parsing the message pattern and handling formatting elements and quoted strings.

In applyPattern, if a registry is present, it manually parses the pattern with a loop, handling quoted strings via the appendQuotedString method. The appendQuotedString method processes quoted substrings starting at a quote character. It treats doubled quotes ("''") as escaped quotes.

However, the appendQuotedString method contains a subtle issue in its condition:

```java
if (escapingOn && c[start] == QUOTE) {
    return appendTo == null ? null : appendTo.append(QUOTE);
}
```

When the current character is a single quote and escaping is enabled, it simply appends a quote and returns immediately without advancing the parsing position. Since the position is not advanced here, the parser does not move forward in the pattern, resulting in an infinite loop in applyPattern while continually encountering the same quote character. This infinite loop causes the OutOfMemoryError as the pattern is never fully consumed.

Therefore, the root cause is that the appendQuotedString method prematurely returns upon encountering a starting quote when escapingOn is true, without advancing the parsing position, leading to unbounded looping in applyPattern.

Fixing this logic to properly consume the escaped quote (e.g., advancing the position after appending the quote) would resolve the infinite loop and prevent the OutOfMemoryError.

This matches the bug description that the issue occurs with a custom registry (thereby calling this parsing code) and a pattern containing single quotes, exactly as in the test case pattern.

Hence, the bug roots from incorrect quote handling in appendQuotedString causing infinite loop and memory exhaustion.

Please advise which methods should be fixed next.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
